photos.alt: Colourful houses and boats along the Nyhavn canal in Copenhagen
Wide lawns and trees in Kongens Have, the King’s Garden, in central Copenhagen

flight.text: Just under 2 hours from UK airports, on average

transfer.text: Metro to the centre in around 15 minutes

stepFree.text: Every metro station has a lift

kidsFare.text: Up to two children under 12 free with each adult ticket

why.text: Ranked the easiest family city break in Europe in the 2026 LateRooms Family Breaks Index, which looked at flight times, airport transfers, walkability and family places to stay.
Prams go free on the metro, buses and trains when there’s space, and buses and trains have marked places for them.
Playgrounds all over the city, and Visit Copenhagen says many are small adventure hubs rather than the usual swings and slide.
Cafés and restaurants commonly have high chairs.

places.name: The King’s Garden playground
places.text: A friendly dragon to ride and a fairy-tale world of wooden figures, in a central park.

places.name: Tower playground, Fælledparken
places.text: Climbing frames shaped like five of the city’s famous towers.

places.name: Experimentarium: Miniverset
places.text: A science play area made for children aged 1 to 5 and their grown-ups.

places.name: Den Blå Planet
places.text: The national aquarium. Fish tanks are hypnotic at any age.

places.name: Copenhagen Zoo
places.text: Big animals and plenty of space to push a buggy.

watch.text: Lifts sometimes close for repairs. The metro’s status page lists any that are out of service, so check it on the day.
Winter days are short and dark. Late spring to early autumn is the easy season for parks and playgrounds.

photos.alt: Formal gardens with a fountain at Schönbrunn Palace, Vienna
A Humboldt penguin at Tiergarten Schönbrunn, Vienna’s zoo

transfer.text: City Airport Train in roughly 16 minutes

kidsFare.text: Under-6s ride free on U-Bahn, trams and buses

why.text: Wiener Linien says every underground station can be reached without steps, using ramps, lifts and raised platforms.
Children travel free on Wiener Linien until the end of the school year in which they turn 6.
A local blog points to central playgrounds at Rathauspark and Karlsplatz, and cafés that are relaxed about toddlers.
Parents who have been describe it as very flat and easy to walk around, with wide pavements.

places.name: ZOOM Ocean
places.text: An under-the-sea play area at the children’s museum, for ages 0 to 6. Book ahead.

places.name: Tiergarten Schönbrunn
places.text: The zoo in the palace grounds, with penguins, pandas and plenty of paths.

places.name: Schönbrunn Palace gardens
places.text: Wide, flat paths for a pram nap after the zoo.

places.name: Prater
places.text: A huge park with the famous big wheel and lots of green space.

watch.text: Lifts are renovated a few at a time, so one may be closed. Wiener Linien suggests changing at a nearby station with a central platform instead.
Heading into the woods outside the city? TravelHealthPro advises everyone to avoid tick bites in Austria.

name: Amsterdam
tagline: The quickest hop, and you can go by train

photos.alt: Canal-side houses and a brick bridge where the Prinsengracht and Reguliersgracht canals meet, Amsterdam
The gate of the Vondelpark in Amsterdam, framed by green leaves

flight.text: Just over 1 hour 20 minutes from UK airports

transfer.text: Train from Schiphol in around 17 minutes

stepFree.text: Pushchairs ride free, with marked spaces on trams and buses

kidsFare.text: Children up to and including 3 travel free

why.text: The shortest flight of the five. Or skip the airport: Eurostar runs direct trains from London, and under-4s travel free on your lap (one per adult).
A parent blog describes it as a relatively flat city where a stroller works fine.
GVB lets you bring a pushchair on board for free; use the marked area and put the brake on.

places.name: Vondelpark
places.text: The big central park, with playgrounds and a paddling pool in summer.

places.name: ARTIS zoo
places.text: A city-centre zoo with an aquarium, easy to reach by tram.

places.name: A canal boat
places.text: Lots of babies love the motion. Ask whether the boat has room for a folded buggy.

watch.text: Cobbles in older streets: Frommer’s says pushing a stroller across them “isn’t much fun”. Stick to main routes, or bring a carrier.
Bikes everywhere. Keep the pram off the red cycle lanes, and look both ways twice.
Canal houses often have very steep stairs. Ask about a lift or ground floor before you book.

name: Valencia
tagline: Sun, sea and a giant playground

photos.alt: Palm-lined paths and lawns in the Turia Garden, Valencia
The giant Gulliver figure with slides, seen from a bridge in Valencia’s Turia Garden

flight.text: Around 2 hours 35 minutes from UK airports

transfer.text: Metro to the centre in roughly 20 minutes

stepFree.text: Flat centre, with a 9 km park running through it

kidsFare.text: Check current child fares with Metrovalencia

why.text: The Turia Garden runs for about 9 km along the old riverbed, with playgrounds, cafés and flat paths: an easy pram walk right through the city.
Gulliver Park is a 70-metre figure of Gulliver that children climb and slide down. Little ones can watch from the edges.
Beach and city in one trip, with milder winters than the other four.

places.name: Gulliver Park
places.text: Free giant playground in the Turia Garden. Go late afternoon, when it’s cooler.

places.name: Bioparc
places.text: Animals in recreated African habitats, at the western end of the Turia Garden.

places.name: Oceanogràfic
places.text: A big aquarium in the City of Arts and Sciences.

places.name: The beach
places.text: Malvarrosa and its neighbours are a short tram or bus ride from the centre.

watch.text: Las Fallas, 1–19 March: a firecracker show (the mascletà) goes off at 2pm every day in the main square, with more fireworks at night. The Local reports it can reach 120 decibels, which the city sees as a health hazard for babies. Avoid these dates, or stay well away and bring ear defenders.
July and August are hot. The NHS advises keeping babies under 6 months out of direct strong sunlight, and the Lullaby Trust says use a clip-on sunshade, not a cover over the pram.

photos.alt: People relaxing on the lawns of the Tiergarten park in Berlin on a sunny day
Panorama of Tempelhofer Feld, the former airport in Berlin that is now a huge open park

flight.text: Just over 2 hours from UK airports

transfer.text: Train from the airport in around 30 minutes

why.text: Ranked second in the LateRooms Family Breaks Index, which counted more than 200 family-friendly attractions.
Under-6s ride free on buses, trams, the U-Bahn and S-Bahn.
A parent blog recommends Prenzlauer Berg for cafés with play corners, so you can have a coffee while they play.

places.name: Tiergarten
places.text: The huge, flat central park. Good for a pram nap on the move.

places.name: Tempelhofer Feld
places.text: A former airport turned park. Endless flat space for new walkers.

places.name: Zoo Berlin
places.text: One of the city’s big days out, right by the Tiergarten.

places.name: Labyrinth Kindermuseum
places.text: A hands-on children’s museum; one blog notes a corner for toddlers.

watch.text: About 1 in 7 U-Bahn stations still has no step-free route, and lifts can be out of order. BVG’s app and journey planner can find step-free routes.
Summers can be hot and winters cold. Spring and early autumn are the comfortable times.
